# Codex Computer Use Reverse Engineering Lab

> Independent, experiment-backed research into the macOS Computer Use stack
> shipped with the Codex desktop app.

Important resources:

- [Project overview](README.md)
- [Current synthesis: V10](reports/v10-target-identity-and-lifetime.md)
- [Report index](reports/README.md)
- [Methodology](docs/00-methodology.md)
- [Reproduction guide](docs/07-reproduction-guide.md)
- [Security threat model](docs/06-security-threat-model.md)
- [Real experiment safety contract](docs/15-real-experiment-safety-contract.md)
- [Full machine-readable project context](llms-full.txt)

Core verified claims:

- The observed Codex path uses deferred tool discovery, `node_repl`, a
  Computer Use wrapper, a Sky JavaScript client, and a native macOS service.
- The checked production fixture contains 21 passing synthetic-app scenarios.
- Native target identity follows canonical app path plus live process lifetime.
- Accepted native actions are not canceled when the JavaScript client times
  out.
- Stale element references and stale screenshot coordinates have materially
  different freshness behavior.

Build-specific reverse-engineering results are evidence, not a public API
contract. The repository is independent and is not an official OpenAI project.
